title: ASIRT investigating after man shot by RCMP officer dies
article: RCMP and the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team are investigating, after officers tried to execute a warrant on the Cold Lake First Nation Thursday.
Police said officers were at the home to arrest an individual when the situation escalated.

"On the afternoon of Thursday, August 15, RCMP officers were conducting investigations involving sexual assaults," ASIRT spokesperson Sarah Jackson said. "[They] had obtained a warrant for an individual's arrest, and a search warrant for the residence he was in.
"This residence was on the Cold Lake First Nation."
A confrontation took place, and RCMP said a 52-year-old man was shot by an officer at the home at about 4:30 p.m. - ASIRT said the man who clashed with police was the subject of the warrants.
"During the confrontation with the male, one RCMP officer fired his service weapon, striking the male," Jackson said.
After he was shot, the man was rushed to the Cold Lake hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
Because an officer was involved in the shooting, police reported the incident to ASIRT, who shed more light on the case later Friday.
Few details on this case were available, although Jackson said ASIRT recovered a knife at the scene of Thursday's altercation - but did not say if the weapon was involved in the incident.
ASIRT is also investigating two other deaths and a non-fatal shooting in recent weeks.

On Aug. 1, RCMP pulled over a suspected impaired driver near Grande Cache northwest of Jasper. Mounties said the man behind the wheel was shot and wounded during an altercation. He fled but was caught a short time later and taken to hospital.
Family later identified the injured man as Curtis Hallock, a regular sidekick on the reality TV show "Mantracker."

The following day, RCMP in Leduc, just south of Edmonton, used a Taser while trying to arrest a suspect in a series of assaults, thefts, driving complaints and hit-and-runs. The 27-year-old went into medical distress while in handcuffs and later died in hospital.
That same weekend, an officer pulled over another suspected impaired driver near Ma Me O Beach on Pigeon Lake southwest of Edmonton.

RCMP said while the officer tried to arrest one of five men inside the car, there was an altercation and two of the occupants were shot. A 30-year-old man from Pigeon Lake died at the scene. His 41-year-old brother was taken to hospital with chest wounds.
In all cases, there's no timeline for ASIRT to make its reports public.
With files from The Canadian Press and CTV's Susan Amerongen
